# SF-O2: What should governments, labs and evaluators disclose about their talks, commitments, evaluations and interventions?

Area O · As of clef 7924 Berichte · Luna 7924 Berichte · JEV 5667 Berichte · amos 7924 Berichte · SubQ 7924 Berichte · drex 7924 Berichte · d3-ultra 5449 Berichte · d3-flash 1674 Berichte

## Subquestions

- [SF-O2-T01](../../fragen/SF-O2/T01/): If government AI talks produce a written record, will it be published in full or only in summary, and which categories of statement (red lines, thresholds, named models) are excluded by default?
- [SF-O2-T02](../../fragen/SF-O2/T02/): Until an official readout of a summit exists, which minimum commitment short of a treaty would each government still publish so that labs and third countries are not left guessing for weeks?
- [SF-O2-T03](../../fragen/SF-O2/T03/): When a government receives or commissions a safety evaluation or an incident report and then classifies it, what may the lab, the evaluator and that government's own officials still publish about its existence and conclusions, and who resolves the disagreement if the evaluator objects to the classification?
- [SF-O2-T04](../../fragen/SF-O2/T04/): Have governments privately asked a lab in their own country to delay, shrink or hold a training run or a release? If so, will they publish how often this happened, under what published criteria and when the request was lifted, without publishing the classified advice itself?
- [SF-O2-T05](../../fragen/SF-O2/T05/): Which of a frontier lab's public commitments are made by the legal entity that would be sued if they are broken, and which only by the research team, and will labs publish this per commitment?
- [SF-O2-T06](../../fragen/SF-O2/T06/): Evaluators with standing access inside a lab are meant to bring verifiability, transparency and a second opinion. Beyond these, what should they publish that is confidential today, such as near-miss incidents or partial evaluations of unpublished models?
- [SF-O2-T07](../../fragen/SF-O2/T07/): What is the first written deliverable of a summit on AI, and by when should it be operational? This was asked about the Trump–Xi meeting.

## Reports by share of levels 4–7

Levels 4–7 / 3–7 = probability each model gives to these levels (3 = useful background or context, 4 = contains some facts that could be cited as evidence … 7 = directly and substantially answers the question). Listed: reports where clef or Luna give levels 3–7 more than 50 %. Sorted by the higher of clef and Luna for levels 4–7. Further models (JEV, amos, d3 …) rated part of the reports; the others show “not yet rated”. The full distribution over the 8 levels is in the data file.
